workflow.critical: Execute ALL steps in exact order — do NOT skip steps
Output base path for all artifacts: {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/
MANDATORY USER REVIEW: After generating each data file, display it in full and WAIT for user confirmation before proceeding. This is a non-negotiable hard stop.
NEVER display passwords in plain text — always mask as ****
SELF-REVIEW RULE: After generating files, execute the quality checklist before reporting complete. Fix all failures.

step.goal: Resolve suite name from argument or active suite in test-suites.yml

check.if: no suite name argument is provided
file does not exist or active_suite is empty
check.output: ❌ No active suite found. Run /aiqa-analyzestory --suite <name> first, then retry.

step.action: Read TestResult/test-suites.yml and find the suite entry where name = {suite_name}

check.output: ❌ Suite "{suite_name}" not found in TestResult/test-suites.yml. Run /aiqa-analyzestory --suite {suite_name} first to register it.

step.action: Confirm the E2E spec exists at: {output_folder}/{story_id}/e2e/tests/{suite_name}.spec.js

step.goal: Verify suite has reached the minimum required status

check.output:
❌ Suite "{suite_name}" is not ready for test data generation. Current status : {current_status} Required status : e2e-generated (minimum)
You must generate E2E tests before generating test data. Run /aiqa-generatee2e first.

step.action: Check {test_users} in config.yaml: - If {test_users} is NOT empty → use saved users directly; proceed to Step 4 - If {test_users} IS empty → ask the user: "I need test user credentials to generate authentication test data. Should I: A) Fetch them from your database automatically ({db_connection_string}) B) You provide them manually one by one Your choice?" Then load and execute workflow: {project-root}/AI-QA-FRAMEWORK/workflows/fetch-test-data/workflow.yaml WAIT for the workflow to complete and {test_users} to be saved before continuing.

step.goal: Self-review — verify artifacts and data quality

artifact-checklist.file: Valid test data — realistic positive input matching the story domain
Edge case data — boundary values, empty, null, max-length, special chars
Security payloads — SQL injection, XSS, CSRF, oversized inputs

quality-checklist.check: All 3 JSON data files exist at the correct paths inside {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/
valid.json contains realistic positive data matching the story's domain — no generic "test123" or "foo" placeholders
valid.json includes user credentials sourced from {test_users} in config.yaml — NOT invented or hardcoded
edge.json covers: empty strings, null values, maximum length strings, special characters (؟!@#), numeric boundaries, zero, negative numbers
security.json contains: SQL injection payloads (' OR '1'='1), XSS payloads (<script>alert(1)</script>), CSRF tokens, oversized inputs
All JSON files are valid parseable JSON — no trailing commas, no unquoted keys
Field names in the JSON match the actual form fields / API request keys used in the spec file — no mismatched names
Expected success/error messages match what the application actually returns — not invented strings

review.fix-if-needed: TD-1 → create any missing JSON file with appropriate content; re-run the generation skill if needed TD-2 → replace generic placeholder values with domain-specific realistic ones TD-3 → populate credentials from config.yaml test_users; never invent credentials TD-4 → add missing edge cases for each field type detected in the story TD-5 → add missing security payload types TD-6 → fix any malformed JSON (trailing commas, unquoted keys, unbalanced braces) TD-7 → cross-reference field names with the spec file and correct any mismatches TD-8 → update expected messages to match actual application behaviour (ask user if uncertain) Save corrected files before proceeding to the user review checkpoint.

step.goal: User review — confirm all 3 data files before any tests run
step.action:
For EACH of the 3 generated data files ({suite_name}-valid.json, {suite_name}-edge.json, {suite_name}-security.json):
1. Display the FULL file content to the user inside a code block 2. Show this message and WAIT:
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ 📋 Test Data Review — {file_name} ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
Please review this data file carefully before running any tests. Wrong or missing values will cause test failures.
❓ Things to check: • Are field names correct for your application's forms/API? • Are the values realistic for your domain (not generic "test123")? • Are credential values, IDs, or keys correct? • Should any REPLACE_WITH_REAL_PASSWORD be replaced with an actual value? • Are the expected success/error messages correct for your system?
Reply: ✅ "OK" / "correct" / "looks good" → I will show you the next file ✏️ Describe what is wrong → I will fix it and show you the corrected version
3. WAIT for user response — do NOT move to the next file until this one is confirmed 4. If user reports issues: a. Apply all corrections to the file on disk b. Display the corrected full content c. Ask: "I've applied your corrections. Does this look right now?" d. WAIT for confirmation e. Repeat until user says OK 5. Move to the next file
Only after ALL 3 files are confirmed by the user → display the completion output
step.output:
✅ Phase 4 Complete — Test Data Generated and Verified
📁 {output_folder}/{story_id}/test-data/ • {suite_name}-valid.json ← positive / happy-path data • {suite_name}-edge.json ← boundary and edge case data • {suite_name}-security.json ← security and injection payloads
All 3 files reviewed and confirmed by user.
Next step → /aiqa-runtests to execute the tests (Phase 5)

step.action: Update the entry: - phases.generate-test-data: done - status: if current rank < rank("test-data-generated") → set to "test-data-generated"; otherwise keep existing (never downgrade) - updated: {current_date}
Write the updated content back to TestResult/test-suites.yml
